## Context

This card changes the VOICE of two operations documents, not their facts. At
BASE neither file names a single alert: `ops/diagnosis.md` opens with "A user
reports the dashboard is not loading their data" and works the flow from what
an operator suspected and typed, and `ops/runbook.md` says in its own Alerting
section that email is the entire alerting chain. Meanwhile the merged t76
`observability/alerts.yaml` carries a real rule set and the merged t83/t84
incident record carries real captured evidence. The gap this card closes is
purely that the documents never tell the operator the truth about how the
incident was actually found: an alert fired, and it left measured evidence
behind.

Three facts the builder needs, each measured at groom against BASE
`67c9db975d75e0e6ae53667c02318a54c2524912`:

1. **The alert name is extracted, never copied.** The fences derive the name
   from the merged files at run time: the t76 `# METRIC-INVENTORY:` line
   yields the `db_fallback_active` gauge, and the unique rule whose `expr`
   mentions that gauge yields the alert name. On the merged tree that chain
   resolves to exactly one rule. The card text and the fences do NOT hand-copy
   that name anywhere it could drift; the fence proves the doc and the rule
   file agree, and a doc that names a rule-shaped identifier the t76 file does
   not declare is RED.
2. **The t41 gate is a hard floor under this card.** The stored merged gate
   index `docs/state/merge_test_index.json` carries the t41 legs that grep
   these exact two files: eight `## <Section>` headers in `ops/diagnosis.md`
   with non-empty regions, the line-anchored
   `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8137/api/v1/health` probe, the fallback /
   `create_db_engine` / runbook mentions, `^## [1-7][.] ` counting EXACTLY 7
   and `^### (Symptom|Cause|Diagnosis|Action)` counting EXACTLY 28 in
   `ops/runbook.md`, and the three generated-row patterns
   (`OPS_DOC_ROWS ... PASS`, `DIAGNOSIS_ROWS ... PASS`,
   `DIAGNOSIS_ENDPOINT ... PASS`) in the generator-owned
   `docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md`. ac1 EXTRACTS those legs from
   the stored index and re-runs them; the card never restates the gate strings,
   so the card cannot soften its own floor.
3. **The evidence this card points at exists and is measured.** The incident
   record `incident-response/incidents/2026-10-17-db-fallback-01/` (its ID is
   extracted by the fence from `incident-response/incidents/README.md`, not
   restated here) holds the merged t83 alert entry and the t84 trio
   `evidence.json`, `response.json`, `resolution.md`. Every path the rewritten
   docs cite must resolve on the tree - ac3 tests each one.

The shape of the rewrite is fixed by the ADD-only constraint: new material
rides INSIDE existing sections as added paragraphs, so the eight diagnosis
headers, the 7x4 runbook counts and the pinned curl line are physically
untouched. The alert-driven material in `ops/diagnosis.md` is labelled as the
extension of the healthy baseline rather than a replacement for it - the
healthy smoke walkthrough stays where it is, byte-identical.

What this card is NOT: it is not a new gate, not a new report row, not a code
change, and not a re-run of the drill. t84 produced the evidence; this card
points at it in the two documents an operator actually reads.

### ac4 - ADD-only purity measured, with the t41 gate strings byte-identical

files the BASE blob (`git cat-file blob <BASE>:<path>` through the cmd.exe

## Verification commands

ac_hash: sha256:bf8de0077992f17e71aad8c9f80adbe2188ad87340225093892f246675754ec9

Five fenced commands, byte-identical to
`evidence.verification_commands.ac1..ac5` in
`docs/state/outputs/t85_definer_groom.json`. The digest is sha256 over the
`JSON.stringify` array of the five FENCED BLOCKS in ac1..ac5 order, each block
taken exactly as it sits between its ```bash fences (the `bash -c '...'`
wrapper INCLUDED) with COMPACT separators and each block CR-stripped and
trimmed - the t58/t62..t84 recipe, so the digest covers the command exactly as
it is pasted rather than a re-derived form. Recomputed from the card on disk by
the grooms assembler (`scratch/t85/probes/assemble.py verify`), which also
re-checks the mirror, so the digest cannot drift from the card.

Each command is a deterministic single `bash -c` one-liner with exactly two
single quotes, no heredoc, no backtick, pure ASCII, run from the repository
root. The python probes travel as base64 literals materialised into a
`mktemp -d` scratch directory and are removed by the fence itself. Each fence
REDs loudly if `python3` is missing - a skipped probe proves nothing about a
rewritten document, and a fence that skips is worse than a fence that fails.
Every probe takes `"$PWD"` and the pinned BASE sha as its two arguments and
prints its own `acN evidence:` lines plus a named `acN RED:` reason per
failing leg, so a failure is self-describing.

### Disclosures (read before editing any fence)

- **ac5 is NON-APPENDABLE.** It pins the literal BASE sha
  `67c9db975d75e0e6ae53667c02318a54c2524912` into the fence as a purity/delta
  leg. The t73..t84 doctrine applies: a BASE-pinned leg may not be re-pinned to
  a moving ref or silently re-based by an append; if the base moves, this card
  is RE-GROOMED, not patched. ac1 carries a BASE-pinned non-vacuity leg with
  the same property. ac2/ac3/ac4 are appendable in the sense that their legs
  are file-content assertions, but ac4s BASE blob comparison shares the same
  pinned sha and moves with it or not at all.
- **Fence semantics are byte-level with CR normalisation.** This worktree runs
  `core.autocrlf=true` with `.gitattributes` absent (measured: `ops/diagnosis.md`
  is 130 CRLF lines / 7348 bytes in the working tree against a 7218-byte LF
  blob). Every comparison in these fences normalises CRLF to LF before
  comparing, so a builder who writes CRLF (which is what the checkout hands
  out) does not fail ac3/ac4, and a builder who rewrites the whole file to LF
  does not fail them either. What cannot pass is a CONTENT change to a pinned
  line.
- **Extraction, never restatement.** The alert name, the incident ID, the eight
  section names, the count regexes, the curl pattern and the generated-row
  shapes are all parsed out of the merged authorities at run time
  (`observability/alerts.yaml`, `incident-response/incidents/README.md`,
  `docs/state/merge_test_index.json`). If an authority changes shape, the
  extraction fails LOUDLY with a named RED reason telling the operator to
  re-groom; it never falls back to a hardcoded value.
- **The 8001 leg measures introduction, not absence.** BASEs own
  `ops/diagnosis.md` already mentions port 8001 once in `## Lessons` ("with
  port 8001 held by a concurrent Docker stack"). A fence that REDs on the
  presence of that string would be wrong about the base, and one that only
  checks absence could never fire on this card. The leg therefore compares the
  OCCURRENCE COUNT against the BASE blob and REDs on growth.
- **Environment.** Windows host, git driven through `cmd.exe /d /c` with ONE
  operation per call (the t65/t82 worktree lesson), no POSIX `&` inside cmd
  strings, no `/dev/null` (cmd wants `nul`). The probes take the WSL-form
  repository root that `"$PWD"` provides and convert with `wslpath -w` for the
  git bridge. `python3` is the interpreter; the probes are stdlib-only and pure
  ASCII.
- **Merge order.** t86 merges BEFORE this card, but no fence here reads any t86
  product: the scan reports are absent at BASE and every leg is written against
  BASE content plus this cards own two files. Nothing in this card depends on a
  t86 artefact existing.

## Constraints (hard - the builder may not drop any of these)

- Exactly 2 product files: `ops/diagnosis.md` and `ops/runbook.md`. Nothing
  else in the product tree may move; ac5 hashes the frozen surface by blob.
- **ADD-only. Zero deleted or reworded lines.** The t41-gate-pinned strings
  listed in Context survive BYTE-IDENTICAL, and ac1 plus ac4 are the pinned
  checks that prove it. The runbook count is EXACTLY 7 sections x EXACTLY 4
  clause headers - adding a numbered section, or a third-level header named
  Symptom/Cause/Diagnosis/Action outside the seven, breaks a merged gate. New
  material rides inside existing sections.
- If the honest alert-driven rewrite CANNOT be ADD-only, the card FAILS and the
  builder escalates. It does not "touch up" a pinned line, and it does not
  delete the healthy baseline to make room.
- The alert name comes from `observability/alerts.yaml` by extraction; the
  incident paths come from the merged t83/t84 tree. Nothing is cited that does
  not exist - ac3 tests every cited path.
- `docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md` is NOT edited by this card (t89
  owns it, and its rows are generator-owned); if the generated rows would move
  because of this cards edits, the card has broken ac1 by definition.
- `docs/backlog.md` and `docs/state/merge_test_index.json` are the orchestrators
  files: never touched, no disclosed-cause route.
- No command in the rewritten docs may contact a non-loopback host; the 8137
  endpoint stays the documented one; port 8001 is never introduced. No secret
  shape of any kind enters either document.
- No product-code change, no `openapi.yaml`, no `README.md`, no
  `ops/logging.md` (the 17-event table is t41-pinned too and this card has no
  reason to touch it), no `observability/` or `incident-response/` change.

## Out of scope

- The t41 gate itself, the generated criteria rows, and the verification
  generator: this card re-runs their legs and edits none of them.
- The t86 scan refresh and any scan-report pointer: t86 merges before this card
  and owns its own documents; no fence here reads a t86 product.
- t88s reconstruction report and t89s evidence map: they consume the rewritten
  docs; none of their files belong in this delta.
- Any change to the alert rule, the metric inventory, the incident record, the
  harness, the backend, or the incident ID.
- Renaming or removing the healthy baseline smoke walkthrough, and any re-run of
  the drill (t84 ran it; this card cites what it produced).
